It is presently not known whether the property (5) is a consequence of the properties (1)–(4). In case $X$ has a second countable topology, (1)–(4) imply (5). Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) (paraphrased): the paper [38] required the M-polyfolds to be second countable; the authors found this requirement unnecessarily restrictive and (5) a better one.

**Proved in Lean.** `HasParacompactOrbitSpace`: Mathlib's `ParacompactSpace` for $|X|$ (no Hausdorff condition). `remark_7_1`: if the object space $X$ is second countable, $|X|$ is paracompact; `hasParacompactOrbitSpace_of_secondCountableTopology`: likewise if $|X|$ is second countable; `hasParacompactOrbitSpace_iff_metrizableSpace`: $|X|$ is paracompact iff it is metrizable.

The tools: `orbitPullback` ($\beta_i = \sigma_i \circ \pi$), `orbitPullback_isSubordinate`, `exists_isSaturated_nhds_finite_orbitPullback`.

### V7.62. Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5): the natural representation, proved in Appendix 7.6.1 (2017 7.5.1)

*restated* · $U_0 := V \cap \bigcap_g s(N_g)$ · contractible $N_g$ not needed

**HWZ (§7.6.1 (2017 §7.5.1), Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) and its proof, pp. 344–346 (2017 pp. 253–254)).** Given an ep-groupoid $X$, an object $x_0 \in X$, and an open neighborhood $V \subset X$ of $x_0$. Then there exist an open neighborhood $U \subset V$ of $x_0$, a group homomorphism $\Phi : G_{x_0} \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U)$, $g \mapsto \Phi(g) = t_g \circ s_g^{-1}$, and an sc-smooth map $\Gamma : G_{x_0} \times U \to \mathbf X$ having the following properties: $\Gamma(g, x_0) = g$; $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$ and $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$ for all $y \in U$ and $g \in G_{x_0}$; if $h : y \to z$ is a morphism connecting two objects $y, z \in U$, then there exists a unique $g \in G_{x_0}$ such that $\Gamma(g, y) = h$. In particular, every morphism between points in $U$ belongs to the image of the map $\Gamma$. The homomorphism $\Phi$ is called a natural representation of the stabilizer group $G_{x_0}$. (In the proof, for every $g \in G_{x_0}$ one chooses contractible open neighborhoods $N^t_g$, $N^s_g$ on which $t$ and $s$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto some open neighborhood $U_0$ of $x_0$, the sets $N^t_g \cup N^s_g$ disjoint; $N_g := N^t_g \cap N^s_g$, $s_g := s|N_g$, $t_g := t|N_g$, and $\Gamma(g, y) = s_g^{-1}(y)$.)

**HWZ (§7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10), p. 346 (2017 p. 255)).** We assume that $X$ is an ep-groupoid with a paracompact orbit space $|X|$ and the object M-polyfold $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity. Suppose further that $x \in X$ and $U(x)$ and $V(x)$ are open neighborhoods of $x$ satisfying $U(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(U(x)) \subset V(x)$ and such that $V(x)$ admits the natural $G_x$-action and $U(x)$ is invariant. If $\beta : X \to [0, 1]$ is a continuous function with support in $U(x)$ and invariant under the $G_x$-action on $V(x)$, then there exists an sc-smooth function $f : X \to [0, \infty)$ with support in $V(x)$, which is, in addition, invariant under the $G_x$-action on $V(x)$ and satisfies $\beta(y) \le f(y)$ for all $y \in X$.

Then there is an sc-smooth $f \ge 0$ with $\mathrm{supp}\,f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}\,U$ and $\mathrm{supp}\,f \subseteq V(x)$, invariant on $V(x)$, with $\beta \le f$.

### V7.67. The proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

*restated* · (4) follows from (1) · the support bound of Lemma 7.6.5 · normalization by bump coverings

**HWZ (§7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2), proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)).** Consider the open covering $(|U_\lambda|)_{\lambda \in \Lambda}$ of $|X|$. For every $x \in X$ take an open neighborhood $V(x)$ with: (1) there exists an open neighborhood $W(x)$ equipped with the natural $G_x$-action such that $V(x) \subset \mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subset W(x)$ and $V(x)$ is invariant; (2) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))) \to X$ is proper; (3) there exists a $\lambda$ with $V(x) \subset U_\lambda$; (4) $(\pi^{-1}(|V(x)|) \setminus V(x)) \cap W(x) = \emptyset$. Take a locally finite refinement $(V'_i)_{i \in I}$ of $(|V(x)|)_{x \in X}$, with $V'_i \subset |V(x_i)|$, open $V''_i$ with $V''_i \subset \mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(V''_i) \subset V'_i$ and $|X| = \bigcup_i V''_i$; $U''_i = V(x_i) \cap \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$ is invariant under the $G_{x_i}$-action, with saturation $U_i = \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$. Take a continuous partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ subordinate to $(V''_i)$; $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ has support in $U''_i \subset V(x_i)$. Using the sc-smooth partitions of unity of $X$, approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ by Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) by an sc-smooth $f_i$ supported in $V(x_i)$ with $f_i \ge (\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$; average using the $G_{x_i}$-action, extend to the saturation of $V(x_i)$ and then by $0$ outside, which gives a function $h_i$ compatible with morphisms. The sum $h$ of all $h_i$ is locally finite and always bigger than $0$, and $(h_i/h)$ is the desired partition of unity for the ep-groupoid $X$.

**Proved in Lean.** `exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen`: inside every open $W \ni x$ there are a natural representation and an open invariant $V \ni x$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,V \subseteq U \subseteq W$ and $\mathrm{cl}\,V$ proper ((1)–(3)); (4) follows: an object of $U$ isomorphic to one of $V$ lies in $V$ (`mem_of_π_mem_image_of_invariant`, `saturation_diff_inter_eq_empty`). `orbitExtension`: the extension of an invariant function on $U$ to the saturation and by $0$, sc-smooth when its support is proper and inside $U$ (`isScSmoothMap_orbitExtension`). `exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn`: for disjoint closed $s, t \subseteq |X|$ there is a continuous $F : |X| \to [0, 1]$, $0$ on $s$ and $1$ on $t$, with $F \circ \pi$ sc-smooth. `admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx`: Part I's normalization through Mathlib's bump coverings. `theorem_7_4` assembles these.

### V8.1. The tangent data (8.1)–(8.9): $T(X, \mathbf X)$ and its structure maps

*restated* · composition by choice, junk elsewhere · $u_T = Tu$, which is (8.8) · $TX$, $T\mathbf X$ in `Type (max u 1)`

**HWZ (§8.1, (8.1)–(8.9), pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258)).** The tangent of the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is the pair $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ (8.1), to be equipped with the structure of an ep-groupoid with object M-polyfold $TX$ and morphism M-polyfold $T\mathbf X$. A tangent vector $(\varphi, h) \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ is viewed as a morphism $(\varphi, h) : Ts(\varphi)(h) \to Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.2), so that $s_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Ts(\varphi)(h)$ and $t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h) = Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.3). If $s_{T\mathbf X}(\psi, k) = Ts(\psi)(k) = Tt(\varphi)(h) = t_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, h)$ (8.4), which implies $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, the multiplication is $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}(Ts(\varphi)(h))) \in T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ (8.5), where $k = Ts(\psi)^{-1}(Tt(\varphi)(h))$; with the projection $\mathbf p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$, shorter, $k \circ h = Ts(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h))^{-1}Ts(\mathbf p(h))(h)$ (8.6). The unit at $a \in T_xX$ is $1_a = (1_x, h_a)$ with $Ts(1_x)(h_a) = a = Tt(1_x)(h_a)$ (8.7), so $u_{T\mathbf X}(a) = (1_x, Ts(1_x)^{-1}(a))$ (8.8), and the inverse map is $\iota_{T\mathbf X}(\varphi, k) = (\varphi^{-1}, T\iota_X(\varphi)(k))$ (8.9).

**Proved in Lean.** `tSrc` $= Ts$, `tTgt` $= Tt$, `tUnit` $= Tu$ and `tInv` $= T\iota$ are Part I's tangent maps (`MPolyfold.tangentMap`) of the structure maps, and `tBase` $= \mathbf p$ is the base point (`MPolyfold.tangentProj`). `tComp k h` is defined by choice: if $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ (then $s(\mathbf p(k)) = t(\mathbf p(h))$, `src_tBase_eq`), it is the vector over $\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h) = Ts(h)$ (`tComp_spec`, `tBase_tComp`, `tSrc_tComp`), which exists (`exists_tSrc_eq`) and is unique, since two vectors with the same base point and the same image under $Ts$ are equal (`tangent_ext`); `tComp_eq` characterizes it, which is (8.5). `tUnit_eq`: $Tu(a)$ is the vector over $1_x$ with $Ts(Tu(a)) = a$, which is (8.8).

### V8.3. Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1): the tangent ep-groupoid $T(X, \mathbf X)$

*restated* · axioms: Lemmas 8.1.3–8.1.8 (V8.5–V8.10) · $(X, \mathbf X)^1$: Chapter 7’s `liftOne`

**HWZ (§8.1, Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), p. 359 (2017 p. 258); proved on pp. 363–365 (2017 pp. 263–264)).** The tangent $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ of the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$, together with the structure maps (8.3)–(8.9), is an ep-groupoid. If $(X, \mathbf X)$ is tame, then also $T(X, \mathbf X)$ is tame. Moreover, the two projections $p : TX \to X^1$ and $\mathbf p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$ together define an sc-smooth functor $(p, \mathbf p) : T(X, \mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)^1$. (The proof assembles Lemmas 8.1.2–8.1.9 (2017: 8.1–8.8); that the projections form a functor "is obvious": $\mathbf p(\varphi, h) = \varphi : s(\varphi) \to t(\varphi)$ is compatible with the composition.)

**Proved in Lean.** `tangentGroupoidStr` is the groupoid of (8.3)–(8.9), and `tangentEpGroupoid` the ep-groupoid on Part I's M-polyfolds $TX$, $T\mathbf X$. `theorem_8_1`: its object and morphism M-polyfolds are $TX$ and $T\mathbf X$, its source, target, unit and inverse are $Ts$, $Tt$, $Tu$, $T\iota$, its composition is `tComp`, a composite $k \circ h$ lies over $\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)$ with source $Ts(h)$, and `tangentProjFunctor`, the ep-functor $(p, \mathbf p) : T(X, \mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)^1$ into Chapter 7's `liftOne`, has the maps $p$ and $\mathbf p$. `theorem_8_1_tame`: if $X$ is tame, so is $TX$.

### V8.12. Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1): the morphisms of $T\mathbf X$ as pairs $(T\varphi, a)$

*narrower* · $G(\varphi, h) = (\varphi, Ts(h))$ · linearity of $T\varphi$: gaps G.7, G.70 · G.70 closed in part

**HWZ (§8.1, Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1), pp. 364 ff. (2017 pp. 264–265)).** There are equivalent ways to turn $T\mathbf X$ into an ep-groupoid. A morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ with $x \in X_1$ has a well-defined associated linear isomorphism $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yY$, the tangent map of $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ at $x$; $(T\varphi, h)$ is a morphism from $h$ to $T\varphi(h)$, and $(T\psi, h) \circ (T\varphi, l) = (T\psi \circ T\varphi, l) = (T(\psi \circ \varphi), l)$ for $h = T\varphi(l)$. The map $G : (\varphi, h) \mapsto (T\varphi, Ts(h))$ is compatible with the functorial structures, and $G : T\mathbf X \to \{(T\varphi, a) \mid \varphi \in \mathbf X_1, a \in T_{s(\varphi)}X\}$ is a bijection; the right-hand side can be given an M-polyfold structure making $G$ an sc-diffeomorphism, and the pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ can be identified with the triples $(a, T\varphi, b)$, $b = T\varphi(a)$. Finally, $Tt(\varphi) \circ Ts(\varphi)^{-1} : T_xX \to T_yX$ is the linearization of $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ at $\varphi$, hence equal to $T\varphi$, and $t_{T\mathbf X} \circ (s_{T\mathbf X}|T_xX)^{-1} = T\varphi : T_xX \to T_yX$ is a linear isomorphism.

**Proved in Lean.** $T\varphi$ is Chapter 7's `tangentMor` (V7.5) and $G$ is `remarkG`, $G(v) = (\mathbf p(v), Ts(v))$. `remark_8_1`: $T\varphi(Ts(v)) = Tt(v)$ for every $v$ over $\varphi$, i.e. $t_T \circ (s_T|T_\varphi\mathbf X)^{-1} = T\varphi$ (`tangentMor_tSrc`); $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$ on $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ (`tangentMor_comp`); $G$ is injective, with range the pairs $(\varphi, a)$ with $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and $a \in T_{s(\varphi)}X$; $Ts(k) = Tt(h)$ iff $Ts(k) = T\mathbf p(h)(Ts(h))$; and $G(k \circ h) = (\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h), Ts(h))$ with $T(\mathbf p(k) \circ \mathbf p(h)) = T\mathbf p(k) \circ T\mathbf p(h)$, so that $G$ is compatible with the compositions.

**HWZ (§8.1, Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1), p. 367 (2017 p. 266)).** If $F, G : X \to Y$ are two sc-smooth functors between the ep-groupoids $X$ and $Y$, then $F$ is naturally equivalent to $G$, $F \simeq G$, if there exists an sc-smooth map $\tau : X \to \mathbf Y$ which associates with every object $x \in X$ a morphism $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ in $\mathbf Y$ such that $\tau(x') \circ F(h) = G(h) \circ \tau(x)$ for every morphism $h : x \to x'$ in $\mathbf X$. The sc-smooth map $\tau$ is called a natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$.

### V8.20. Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4): strong bundles over ep-groupoids

*restated* · surjectivity kept, follows from (2)

**HWZ (§8.3, Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4), p. 375 (2017 p. 271)).** A strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $X$ is a pair $(P, \mu)$ in which $P : W \to X$ is a strong bundle over the object M-polyfold $X$ and $\mu : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_P\,W \to W$ is a strong bundle map covering the target map $t : \mathbf X \to X$, so that $P \circ \mu(\psi, w) = t(\psi)$, such that (1) $\mu$ is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism and linear on the fibres $W_x$; (2) $\mu(1_x, w) = w$ for all $x \in X$ and $w \in W_x$; (3) $\mu(\psi \circ \gamma, w) = \mu(\psi, \mu(\gamma, w))$ for all $\psi, \gamma \in \mathbf X$ and $w \in W$ with $s(\gamma) = P(w)$ and $t(\gamma) = s(\psi) = P(\mu(\gamma, w))$.

### V8.24. Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6): strong bundle functors

*restated* · three conditions read as two

### V8.25. Definitions 8.3.2 and 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5 and 8.6) are equivalent

### V8.26. Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7): section functors

*restated* · “vector space”: closure, no `Module` · (3) in the germ reading

**HWZ (§8.3, Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7), pp. 379 ff. (2017 pp. 274–275)).** Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over the ep-groupoid $X$. (1) An sc-smooth section functor $f$ is an sc-smooth section $f : X \to W$ of $P$ satisfying the functorial condition $f(y) = \mu(\varphi, f(x))$ for morphisms $\varphi : x \to y$; $\Gamma(P, \mu)$ is the vector space of sc-smooth section functors. (2) An sc⁺-section functor is an $f \in \Gamma(P, \mu)$ with $f(x) \in W_{0,1}$ for all $x$ which, viewed as a section of $W[1] \to X$, is sc-smooth; $\Gamma^+(P, \mu) \subset \Gamma(P, \mu)$ is the vector subspace of sc⁺-section functors. (3) An sc-Fredholm section functor is an $f \in \Gamma(P, \mu)$ which, as a section of $W \to X$, is an sc-Fredholm section; $\mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$ is the collection of these.

**Proved in Lean.** `IsFunctorialSection`: $f(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, f(s(\varphi)))$ for every morphism. `IsScSmoothSectionFunctor`, `IsScPlusSectionFunctor`, `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor`: (1)–(3), with Part I's sc-smooth, sc⁺- and sc-Fredholm sections; `sectionFunctors` $= \Gamma(P, \mu)$, `plusSectionFunctors` $= \Gamma^+(P, \mu)$, `fredholmSectionFunctors` $= \mathrm{Fred}(P, \mu)$, with `plusSectionFunctors_subset`, `fredholmSectionFunctors_subset`. $\Gamma(P, \mu)$ and $\Gamma^+(P, \mu)$ contain the zero section and are closed under sums and constant multiples (`fiberZero_mem_sectionFunctors`, `sectionAdd_mem_sectionFunctors`, `sectionSmul_mem_sectionFunctors`, `fiberZero_mem_plusSectionFunctors`, `sectionAdd_mem_plusSectionFunctors`, `sectionSmul_mem_plusSectionFunctors`), from the same facts for Part I's sections (`StrongBundle.isScSmoothSection_fiberZero`, `StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.sectionAdd_of_isScSmoothSection`, `StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.sectionSmul_const`).

### V8.27. Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8): proper covering functors

*restated* · $U(x)$ open; local inverses $\sigma(y)$ · (3) on Part I’s fibred product

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), p. 383 (2017 p. 275)).** An sc-smooth functor $F : Y \to X$ between ep-groupoids is a proper covering functor if (1) the sc-smooth map $F : Y \to X$ between the objects is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism; (2) for every object $x \in X$ the preimage $F^{-1}(x)$ is finite, and there exist an open neighborhood $U(x)$ and mutually disjoint open neighborhoods $U(y)$ of the points $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ such that $F : U(y) \to U(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism and $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigcup_{y \in F^{-1}(x)} U(y)$; (3) the map $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is an sc-diffeomorphism.

**Proved in Lean.** `EpFunctor.IsProperCovering F`: (1) `surjective`, `isLocalScDiffeo`; (2) `finite_fiber`, and `evenlyCovered`: an open $U \ni x$ and pairwise disjoint $V(y) \ni y$ with sc-diffeomorphisms $F : V(y) \to U$ (inverses $\sigma(y)$) and $F^{-1}(U) = \bigcup_y V(y)$; (3) `isScDiffeo_fibredMap`: `fibredMap`, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, is an sc-diffeomorphism onto Part I's fibred-product sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times Y$ (`MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`) (fields of the structure). `isProperCovering_id`: the identity functor of every ep-groupoid is one.

### V8.28. The degeneracy index of $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$ (after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8))

*narrower* · hidden: $X$, $Y$ tame · in general only $\le$

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8), pp. 383 ff. (2017 pp. 275–276)).** The sc-diffeomorphism $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\varphi \mapsto (F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, preserves the degeneracy index, so $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$. The fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X \times Y$, which has the degeneracy index $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(\varphi, y) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) + d_Y(y)$. Since $F$ and $s$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) + d_Y(s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$, hence $d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = \tfrac12\,d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$: the fibred product lies in a particular position in the full product.

**Proved in Lean.** `IsProperCovering.degIndex_fibredMap`: $d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, by Part I's invariance of the degeneracy index under sc-diffeomorphisms (`proposition_2_24`); `IsProperCovering.degIndex_mor`: $d_{\mathbf X}(F(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$. In general, `IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap_le`: $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) \le 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$, from Part I's `MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le`. **For tame $X$ and $Y$**, `IsProperCovering.degIndex_prod_fibredMap`: $d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = 2\,d_{\mathbf Y}(\varphi)$ and $2\,d_{\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X \times Y}(F(\varphi), s(\varphi))$, from Part I's product formula for tame M-polyfolds (`MPolyfold.isTame_prod`).

### V8.32. Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9): $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$, covering functors and geometric lifts

*restated* · $C$ = `SingleObj G`; $D$, $G$ in `Type` · finiteness where it is used · $D = \emptyset$ allowed

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) and the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ before it, pp. 387–389 (2017 pp. 279–280)).** $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ is the category whose objects are M-polyfolds and whose morphisms are sc-smooth diffeomorphisms between M-polyfolds. Let $D$ and $C$ be two categories with finitely many objects and morphisms, all morphisms isomorphisms, $C$ with only one object $x$. A covering functor $f : D \to C$ is a functor such that $\mathbf D \to \mathbf C\,{}_s{\times}_f\,D$, $\psi \mapsto (f(\psi), s(\psi))$, is a bijection. A geometric lift of a covering functor $f : D \to C$ consists of two functors $L_D : D \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ and $L_C : C \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$ and a natural transformation $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$ of the functors $L_D, L_C \circ f : D \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$.

**Proved in Lean.** `MPolyfoldCat`: bundled M-polyfolds (on Hausdorff paracompact spaces) of one universe; `ScDiffeo A B`: sc-diffeomorphisms with their inverses, with `ScDiffeo.id`, `ScDiffeo.comp`, `ScDiffeo.ext`: the category $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$. For a groupoid $D$ in `Type` and a group $G$ in `Type`, with $C$ = `SingleObj G`: `coveringMap f` maps $\psi : a \to b$ to $(f(\psi), a) \in G \times D$, and `IsCoveringFunctor f` says it is bijective; `IsCoveringFunctor.existsUnique_lift`, `IsCoveringFunctor.lift`: the unique $\psi$ with given $f(\psi)$ and source. `GeometricLift f`: functors `LD`, `LC` into `MPolyfoldCat` and a natural transformation `τ` $: L_D \to L_C \circ f$. `isCoveringFunctor_of_isEmpty`: every functor from an empty $D$ is a covering functor; `CoveringExamples.isCoveringFunctor_id`: a witness.

### V8.33. After Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9): the maps $\varphi_{yy'}$, the actions and the equivariance of $\tau(y)$

*as in the book*

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), after Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9), pp. 388–390 (2017 pp. 280–281)).** For a covering functor $f : D \to C$ with a geometric lift $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$: $U(x) := L_C(x)$ and $U(y) := L_D(y)$ for $y \in D = f^{-1}(x)$; $\tau(y) : U(y) \to U(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; for $\psi : y \to y'$, $\varphi_{yy'}(\psi) := L_D(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$ is an sc-diffeomorphism, and $\varphi_{yy''}(\psi \circ \gamma) = \varphi_{y'y''}(\psi) \circ \varphi_{yy'}(\gamma)$. $G_y$ acts on $U(y)$ by $h \ast z := L_D(h)(z)$ and $G_x$ on $U(x)$ by $g \ast z = L_C(g)(z)$, and since $\tau$ is natural, $\tau(y)(h \ast z) = f(h) \ast \tau(y)(z)$: the $\tau(y)$ are equivariant with respect to $f : G_y \to G_x$.

**Proved in Lean.** `GeometricLift.Ux` $= U(x)$; `τy y` $= \tau(y)$, an sc-diffeomorphism (`isScDiffeoOn_τy`); `φ ψ` $= \varphi_{yy'}(\psi)$, an sc-diffeomorphism (`isScDiffeoOn_φ`), functorial (`φ_comp`, `φ_id`, `φ_inv_φ`); the actions (`smul_def`, `smul_def'`), sc-smooth (`isScSmoothMap_smul`); `τy_φ`: $\tau(y')(\varphi_{yy'}(\psi)(z)) = f(\psi) \ast \tau(y)(z)$; `τ_equivariant`: $\tau(y)(h \ast z) = f(h) \ast \tau(y)(z)$ for $h \in G_y$.

*narrower* · hidden: $D$ nonempty · “one verifies”: carried out · inverse of (8.16) sc-smooth directly

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) and its proof, pp. 389–391 (2017 pp. 281–282)).** Associated with a covering functor $f : D \to C$ and a geometric lift $\tau : L_D \to L_C \circ f$ of $f$ there is a natural construction of a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ between two ep-groupoids. (Construction: $X = G_x \ltimes U(x)$, with $s(g, z) = z$, $t(g, z) = g \ast z$; $Y = \bigcup_{y \in D} U(y)$ and $\mathbf Y = \bigcup_{(y, y') \in D \times D} [\mathrm{mor}(y, y') \times U(y)]$, with $s(\psi, z) = z$, $t(\psi, z) = \varphi_{yy'}(\psi)(z)$, $(\psi, z') \circ (\gamma, z) = (\psi \circ \gamma, z)$, units $(1_y, z)$ and inverses $(\psi^{-1}, \varphi_{yy'}(\psi)(z))$, and "one verifies" that $Y$ is an ep-groupoid; $F|U(y) := \tau(y)$ and $F(\psi, z) = (f(\psi), \tau(y)(z))$. The map (8.16) $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $(\psi, z) \mapsto ((f(\psi), F(z)), z)$, is a bijection, by the definition of a covering functor, and a local sc-diffeomorphism, hence an sc-diffeomorphism.)

### V8.36. Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (Proper Covering II): the local model of a proper covering functor

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) and its proof, 2017 pp. 283–284).** Let $F : Y \to X$ be a proper covering functor and fix $x \in X$; let $C$ be the full subcategory of $X$ with the single object $x$ and the morphisms $G_x$, and $D$ the full subcategory with the finite object set $F^{-1}(x)$. Given a sufficiently small open neighborhood $U(x)$ of $x$ as in Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5), there exist a geometric lift $A : K \to L$ of $f$ and fully faithful open embedding functors $\Phi : L \to X$ and $\Psi : K \to Y$, the image of $\Phi$ the full subcategory associated with $U(x)$ and the image of $\Psi$ the full subcategory associated with $F^{-1}(U(x))$, such that $F \circ \Psi = \Phi \circ A$. (In the proof, $L_C(x) = U(x)$, $L_C(g) = \Phi(g)$, $L_D(y) = U(y)$, $L_D(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi_0))^{-1}$ for $\psi : y \to y'$ in $\mathbf U(\psi_0)$, and $\tau(y) = F|U(y)$; "one verifies" that this is a geometric lift, and $A : K \to L$, $L = G_x \ltimes U(x)$, is its functor of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3).)

### V8.37. Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10): proper strong bundle covering functors

*restated* · $A$ a strong bundle functor · (3) on a pull-back: a reading

**HWZ (§8.5 (2017 §8.4), Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10), p. 394 (2017 p. 285)).** Let $(W, \mu)$ and $(V, \tau)$ be strong bundles over the ep-groupoids $Y$ and $X$, $P : W \to Y$ and $Q : V \to X$. A proper strong bundle covering functor is a strong bundle map $A$ (in particular fibrewise linear) with $Q \circ A = F \circ P$ and (1) $A$ is surjective and a local strong bundle isomorphism covering an sc-smooth proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$; (2) $F^{-1}(x)$ is finite for every $x \in X$, and there are open neighborhoods $U(x)$ and mutually disjoint $U(y)$, $y \in F^{-1}(x)$, such that $A : W|U(y) \to V|U(x)$ is a strong bundle isomorphism for every $y \in F^{-1}(x)$ and $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigcup_{y \in F^{-1}(x)} U(y)$; (3) the map $\mathbf W \to \mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W$, $(\psi, w) \mapsto ((F(\psi), A(w)), w)$, is a strong bundle isomorphism covering the sc-diffeomorphism $\mathbf Y \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$, $\psi \mapsto (F(\psi), s(\psi))$, where the strong bundle projection $\mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y$ is $((\varphi, v), w) \mapsto (\varphi, P(w))$.

**Proved in Lean.** `IsProperStrongBundleCovering EW EV F A`, for an ep-functor $A$ between the ep-groupoids of V8.22: $A$ is a strong bundle functor covering $F$ (Definition 8.3.3 (2017: 8.6), V8.24; `isStrongBundleFunctor`), surjective on objects, and $F$ is a proper covering functor; (1) $A$ is a strong bundle isomorphism (`StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn`, with fibre isomorphisms `IsStrongBundleIsoOn.fiberEquiv`) near every $y$; (2) over an even covering of every $x$; (3) `fibredLift`, $(\psi, w) \mapsto ((F(\psi), A(w)), w)$, is a strong bundle isomorphism from the pull-back $\mathbf W$ onto the pull-back of $P$ along $\mathrm{pr}_2 : \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_F\,Y \to Y$ (`EpFunctor.fibredSnd`, `EpFunctor.isScSmoothMap_fibredSnd`), covering $\psi \mapsto (F(\psi), s(\psi))$ (fields). `fibredBundleEquiv`: that pull-back is $\mathbf V\,{}_s{\times}_A\,W$, with the text's projection (`pullbackProj_fibredBundleEquiv`, `fibredBundleEquiv_symm_fibredLift`). Witnesses: `isProperStrongBundleCovering_id`, `TrivialBundle.epBundle_isProperStrongBundleCovering`.

### V8.42. Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4): the number of sheets is constant on components of $|X|$

*restated* · $\mathbb N$ with $0$; the values are $\ge 1$ · only local constancy used

**HWZ (§8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1), Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4) and the paragraph before it, 2017 p. 288).** The structure of isomorphism classes of $F^{-1}(x)$ stays the same if $x$ is perturbed, which follows from the definition of a proper covering functor; together with Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11) this gives: let $F : Y \to X$ be an sc-smooth proper covering functor. Then for every connected component $c$ of the orbit space $|X|$ there is a constant $k_c$ such that $\#F^{-1}(x) = k_c$ whenever $\pi(x) \in c$. In other words, viewing $\mathbb N = \{1, 2, \dots\}$ as an ep-groupoid with the identities as the morphisms, the map $X \to \mathbb N$, $x \mapsto \#F^{-1}(x)$, is an sc-smooth functor.

**Proved in Lean.** `IsProperCovering.proposition_8_4`: for every connected component $c$ of $|X|$ there is $k$ with $\#F^{-1}(x) = k$ for all $x$ with $\pi(x) \in c$. The proof: $\#F^{-1}(x) \ge 1$ (`IsProperCovering.one_le_ncard_fiber`), locally constant on $X$ (`IsProperCovering.eventually_ncard_fiber_eq`, `IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_ncard_fiber`) and constant on isomorphism classes (Lemma 8.6.3 (2017: 8.11)), hence a locally constant function on $|X|$ (`IsProperCovering.fiberCardOrbit`, `IsProperCovering.isLocallyConstant_fiberCardOrbit`). `IsProperCovering.fiberCardFunctor`: $x \mapsto \#F^{-1}(x)$ is an ep-functor into the trivial ep-groupoid (`EpGroupoid.trivial`) of the discrete M-polyfold $\mathbb N$ (`discretePolyfold`).

### V8.43. §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2): the structure of strong bundle coverings

*restated* · natural transformation as its identity

**HWZ (§8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2), 2017 pp. 288–289).** For a proper strong bundle covering functor $A$ as in Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10), with $Q \circ A = F \circ P$: a strong bundle $P : W \to Y$ over an ep-groupoid comes with $\mu_Y$, associating with a morphism $\varphi : y \to y'$ a topological linear isomorphism $\mu_Y(\varphi) : P^{-1}(y) \to P^{-1}(y')$, a morphism $w \to w'$ being a pair $(\varphi, w) : w \to \mu_Y(\varphi)(w)$; the same holds for $Q : V \to X$. On morphisms $A(\varphi, w) = (F(\varphi), A_{s(\varphi)}(w))$, where $A_y : P^{-1}(y) \to Q^{-1}(F(y))$ is the topological linear isomorphism induced by $A$, and $t(A(\varphi, w)) = A(t(\varphi, w))$ gives $\mu_X(F(\varphi)) \circ A_{s(\varphi)} = A_{t(\varphi)} \circ \mu_Y(\varphi)$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf Y$. With $\mathrm{Ban}$ the category of Banach spaces and topological linear isomorphisms, $\mu_Y : Y \to \mathrm{Ban}$ and $\mu_X : X \to \mathrm{Ban}$ are functors, and $y \mapsto A_y$ is a natural transformation $\mu_Y \to \mu_X \circ F$.

**Proved in Lean.** `IsProperStrongBundleCovering.mor_val`: $A(\varphi, w) = (F(\varphi), A(w))$; `IsProperStrongBundleCovering.fiberEquiv y`: $A_y : W_y \to V_{F(y)}$, a topological linear isomorphism; `IsStrongBundleFunctor.μ_comm`: $\mu_X(F(\varphi), A(w)) = A(\mu_Y(\varphi, w))$; `section_8_5_2`: $\mu_X(F(\varphi)) \circ A_{s(\varphi)} = A_{t(\varphi)} \circ \mu_Y(\varphi)$ on $W_{s(\varphi)}$, for every morphism $\varphi$ of $Y$.

### V9.1. Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids

*restated* · paracompactness as an instance · properness: `IsProperMap` of the inclusion · 2017 "(ii) and (iii)": possible misprint

**HWZ (§9.1, Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292)).** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the ep-groupoid $X$ is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ with (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) = \{\Theta > 0\}$ contained in $X_\infty$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact in the topology induced from $|X|$; and, at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, (2) an open $U(x)$ and finitely many submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, (3) weights $\sigma_i \in \mathbb Q$, $\sigma_i > 0$, and (4) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ for $y \in U(x)$: a local branching structure.

**Proved in Lean.** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples.

### V9.2. Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$

*narrower* · dimension measured in a chart (G.7) · local constancy: hypothesis, ℝᵐ proved · footnote not formalized (G.93)

**HWZ (§9.1, Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291), and Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph, p. 402).** The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$, the local dimension of $M$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support the manifolds of a local branching structure can be taken $n$-dimensional (2017: are $n$-dimensional); by a footnote (new in 2021) an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if small structures have sheets of one dimension.

**Proved in Lean.** A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$. The dimensions of the $M_i$ of one structure through $x$ are determined.

### V9.9. Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2), the dimensional decomposition

*narrower* · uniqueness: does not hold as we read it · counterexample: $1_L$ on ℝ² · global gluing open (G.96)

**HWZ (§9.1, Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297)).** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ determines a unique sequence $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \ldots$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids characterized by (1) $\Theta_k$ is $k$-dimensional and (2) $\Theta = \Theta_0 + \Theta_1 + \cdots$, the sum locally finite. Proof: at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ take a symmetric structure, split $I = I_0 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I_n$ by the dimension of the $M_i$ and put $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{i \in I_k, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$; independence of the structure is Proposition 9.1.12.

**Proved in Lean.** For a local branching structure with dimension labelling, $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{\dim M_i = k,\, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ is represented on $U(x)$ by the $k$-dimensional structure $(M_i)_{\dim M_i = k}$, $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$, and for a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension and $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant. The statement of the proposition, "a unique family $(\Theta_k)$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional, with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ pointwise, and every such family locally finite", is `Proposition_9_1_11`; on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ it does not hold as we read it: for the indicator $\Theta$ of the $x$-axis $L$, both $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ and $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ are such families. Uniqueness among local decompositions, those given near every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ by the dimensional parts of a local branching structure (the form the proof builds): two such decompositions are equal, given Proposition 9.1.12, hence over $\mathbb R^m$ with no hypothesis and under the graph representation in general; in the example, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ is local and the other decomposition is not.

**HWZ (§9.2, the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$, p. 409 (2017 pp. 297–298)).** For a smooth $x$, $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums $\sum \sigma_L L$ of finite-dimensional linear subspaces $L \subseteq T_xX$ with rational weights; a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ maps them by $T\varphi$; $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ is the category of pairs $(x, a)$, with the projection $\pi : \mathrm{Gr}(X) \to X^\infty$.

**Proved in Lean.** $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums $\sum_L \sigma_L L$, $\sigma_L \in \mathbb Q$, of subsets $L$ of $T_xX$; a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of $X^\infty$ pushes them forward by the tangent $T\varphi$ of Chapter 7, functorially; the objects $(x, a)$, $a \in \mathrm{Gr}(x)$, and the pairs $(a, \varphi)$ form a category with the projection functor $\pi$ to the full subcategory $X^\infty$ of smooth objects.

### V9.42. Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13), essential in $M_i$ iff essential in $M_{i'}$

**HWZ (§9.4, Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317)).** If $z \in K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_i$, it is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_{i'}$; so $K(i, i')^e$, $K(i, i')^{ne}$ do not depend on the reference sheet (proof left to the reader).

### V10.1. Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1), equivalences and the class $E$

*as in the book* · as stated · witness: pair groupoid of ℤ → point

**HWZ (§10.1, Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017: Definition 10.1, p. 333)).** An equivalence $F : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an sc-smooth functor which is faithful and full, induces a homeomorphism $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$, and is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects; $E$ is the class of equivalences.

**Proved in Lean.** A structure on an sc-smooth functor with four fields: full, faithful, $|F|$ a homeomorphism, $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The class `EP.equivalences` contains the identities and is closed under composition; an equivalence is essentially surjective, and the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is an equivalence.

### G.1. Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2): the weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$

*not formalized*

**HWZ (§1.1, Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2), pp. 6 ff. (preprint pp. 6–7)).** With $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, the spaces $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$ of $L^2$ functions whose weak derivatives up to order $m$, weighted by $e^{\delta_m|s|}$, are in $L^2$ form an sc-structure on $L^2(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, "using Sobolev's compact embedding theorem for bounded domains and the assumption that $(\delta_m)$ is strictly increasing".

**Proved in Lean.** **Not formalized.** Mathlib has no weighted Sobolev spaces and no Rellich–Kondrachov theorem; the exposition proves the example in full (Proposition 1.C). The only examples of sc-Banach spaces built here are the constant structure on a finite-dimensional space, and the sums, shifts, sc-subspaces and quotients of sc-Banach spaces (V1.1, V1.4, V1.6). This example, with the shift map of the 2010 paper, is the project's planned step H2.


### G.2. Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15): partial cones in place of partial quadrants

*not formalized*

**HWZ (§1.1, Remark 1.1.17 (preprint 1.15), p. 10 (preprint p. 11)).** Instead of a partial quadrant $C$ one may take a closed convex partial cone $P$ ($\lambda P \subset P$ for $\lambda \ge 0$) with non-empty interior; for $U$ open in $P$, $\mathrm{sc}^1$ is defined as in Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), with the tangent map on $TP = P^1 \oplus E$, again a closed cone with non-empty interior. Many results should carry over, "but one should check carefully which arguments carry over".

**Proved in Lean.** **Not formalized**, as in the exposition, which stays with quadrants. The proofs of §§1.2–1.3 use of the quadrant only the sc-domain property (V1.27: open-in-convex level sets with unique derivatives), so they apply to any $U$ with that property; whether relatively open subsets of partial cones have it is not examined. (Proposition 1.2.4 and Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint Propositions 1.19 and 1.20) under the text's hypothesis, listed here until 2026-10-25, are now proved as stated, V1.18–V1.19.)


### G.3. Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14): $Df$ need not be norm continuous

*formalized since* · now V1.13 · now V1.34

**HWZ (§1.1, after Definition 1.1.15 (preprint 1.14), preprint p. 11).** "In general, the map $U_1 \to \mathcal L(E_0, F_0)$, defined by $x \mapsto Df(x)$, will not(!) be continuous, if the space of bounded linear operators is equipped with the operator norm."

**Proved in Lean.** **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (third addendum; V1.13, V1.34), by an example (the text gives none). $X$ is the sc-Banach space of sequences whose level $m$ consists of the $x$ with $(k+1)^m x_k \to 0$, normed by $|x|_m = \sup_k (k+1)^m|x_k|$: every level is a copy of $c_0$, the inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1/(k+1))$, compact, and the finitely supported sequences are smooth points dense in every level. On $E = \mathbb R \oplus X$ the map $f(t, x)_k = \cos(kt)x_k$ is $\mathrm{sc}^1$ with $Df(t, x)(\tau, \xi)_k = -k\sin(kt)x_k\tau + \cos(kt)\xi_k$ (the factor $k$ is absorbed by one level). $(\pi/(n+1), 0) \to 0$ in $E_1$, but $\|Df(\pi/(n+1), 0) - Df(0, 0)\| \ge 2$ (test on the unit vector $e_{n+1}$); since the derivative is unique on $E_1$, no derivative family of $f$ is continuous for the operator norm. Not formalized: that $f$ is sc-smooth (it is), and the shift map of the exposition (§6), which needs Example 1.1.3 (preprint 1.2) (G.1).

### G.31. Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3): “$X^1 \ne X$ is possible”

*formalized since* · now V4.6

**HWZ (§4.1, Remark 4.1.3 (preprint 4.3), p. 176 (preprint p. 148)).** If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".

**Proved in Lean.** **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (fourth addendum; V4.6), by an example the preprint and 2017 texts do not give. The 2021 edition (p. 176) adds an example: the space of its Subsection 1.4.4 (a line with a half-plane attached), made an M-polyfold with $X_\infty = X$, for which $1_0^1$ cannot be sc-smooth, since Theorem 4.1.2 (preprint 4.2) would make $X$ a manifold of constant local dimension; that argument holds as we read it and is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, item 159). On the weighted sequence space $X$ of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k+1)^m|x_k|$), $L(t)$ is the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k = 2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t) = 0$ for $t \le 0$. The retraction $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$ of $\mathbb R \oplus X$ is sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss; its retract $O$ consists of smooth points, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.1.8 (preprint 4.8)), and the M-polyfold $O$ with its single chart has $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ not sc-smooth. Why an example needs a retraction that loses a level (one with $C^1$ level maps gives none) is an argument, not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

### G.74. Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3): sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex

*not formalized*

**HWZ (§8.2, Definitions 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2 and 8.3), pp. 372–375 (2017 pp. 268–270)).** Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2): an sc-differential $k$-form on the ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$ is an sc-smooth map $\omega : \oplus^k TX \to \mathbb R$ on the Whitney sum of the tangent of the object M-polyfold, linear in each argument and skew-symmetric, with $(T\varphi)^*\omega_y = \omega_x$ for every morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ in $\mathbf X_1$; $\Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is the vector space of these forms. A form on $X^i$ is a form on $X^{i+1}$, and $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is the direct limit of the directed system $\Omega^*_{ep}(X^i) \to \Omega^*_{ep}(X^k)$, $i \le k$. The exterior derivative is $d[\omega] := [d\omega]$, with $d\omega$ compatible with morphisms and $d \circ d = 0$. Definition 8.2.2 (2017: 8.3): $(\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X), d)$ is the sc-de Rham complex of the ep-groupoid $X$.

**Proved in Lean.** **Not formalized.** It needs the Whitney sums $\oplus^k TX$ as M-polyfolds, the linear structure of $T_xX$ (gap G.7), linear maps $T\varphi$ (gap G.70), the M-polyfolds $X^i$ for $i \ge 2$ (gap G.6, closed since: V2.93, V2.97) and the sc-differential forms, the Lie bracket and the exterior derivative of Part I's §4.4 (gaps G.37–G.39), which are not formalized; the Lie bracket on an M-polyfold is formalized since (V4.76, gap G.38 closed). Nothing else in Chapter 8 depends on it. Definition 8.2.1 (2017: 8.2) writes $T_yY$ for $T_yX$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 8, item 110).

### G.123. the transitivity of the equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles, the composition in $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and the strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10

*formalized since* · now V10.68 · now V10.69 · now V10.70 · now V10.71

**HWZ (§10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364), Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366), and Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition)).** Equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles is an equivalence relation, generalized strong bundle maps compose to a category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$, and a generalized strong bundle map is invertible iff it is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences.

**Proved in Lean.** **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V10.68–V10.71), except the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10. The weak fibred product of strong bundles is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$ (V10.68), the equivalence of diagrams is transitive (V10.69), and the composition makes $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ a category (V10.70, V10.55); a diagram with both legs strong bundle equivalences represents an isomorphism (V10.71). Still open: that an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is represented with both legs strong bundle equivalences, proved for the base functor only; for the strong bundle functor it would need strong bundle versions of the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2 (Findings, Chapter 10, items 18, 19, 50, 53).
